lines: The wind came in <wavy>hard enough</wavy> to make the whole village taste like dust.
No rain here, just grit in the shutters and everyone checking their eyes.
The sand got everywhere, but people found their way indoors.
Harsh wind can scare a village nearly as well as thunder. We are still here.
We are sweeping doorways and counting heads after that wall of dust.
The wind threw sand at the windows. I did not like the sound.
I got dust in my mouth even inside. How does it do that?
The grown-ups said cover my face, so I did.
It was like the ground tried to <wavy>fly away</wavy>.
I am okay, but my hair feels crunchy.
The snow came down hard, but the hearths held and the doors stayed shut.
Cold frightens <pulse>slowly</pulse>. We are checking fingers, roofs, and firewood.
The village went white and quiet for a while. <italic>Quiet is not always peace.</italic>
Everyone is chilled, but accounted for. Warmth matters now.
We are clearing paths before the snow hides what people need.
